subject: Limited export & observability clause — sign-off required for BrightLayer DPA redlines
messages:
From: Tom Bennett <tbennett@brightlayer.co>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightLayer Legal <legal@brightlayer.co>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Mike —

Thanks for the call earlier. We're attaching our latest redlines to the DPA (BrightLayer_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf). Two primary asks from our side:

1) Observability export exception — we need aggregated request telemetry (latency, error codes, model-id) exported to our analytics vendor MetricX for product analytics. MetricX will receive only aggregated metrics (no user identifiers).
2) Affirmation that runtime telemetry will not be used to train models; however, we need the option to request limited analytics-derived features (e.g., feature flags) that may require low-granularity hashes for debugging.

From a procurement timeline perspective we need final legal sign-off by end of next week (9/19) to match our SOW. Please advise what changes Redwood needs internally to accept these redlines.

Attachment: BrightLayer_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Bennett
Head of Platform Partnerships — BrightLayer
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Forwarding BrightLayer's redlines — they pushed back on training-use prohibition and request an observability export to MetricX (aggregated metrics only). They need sign-off by 9/19 for SOW.

High-level ask for Product/Security: can we accept an export carveout that:
- restricts exports to aggregated, non-identifiable metrics (latency, error codes, model id)
- requires MetricX contract + SOC2 evidence and only accepts metrics at a 1-minute rollup
- keeps a strict no-training clause for model telemetry (unless explicitly consented later) but allows hashed debug tokens for short-term debugging (ephemeral, non-identifying)

Olga — curious if legal wants different language; Priya/Irene can you confirm technical and risk constraints? If we can propose a redline today I will run to the account.

— Mike
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Mike — thanks for loop-in. A few clarifying questions before we draft language:

1) "Aggregated" — what roll-up window are they expecting? 1 minute vs 1 hour has different KV/cache implications and will affect our telemetry pipeline.
2) "Model-id" — do they need a stable model version identifier (e.g., model-v1.3) for observability, or is a hashed short id acceptable? Stable identifiers increase fingerprinting risk.
3) "Hashed debug tokens" — we need to know if these are reversible or used to rehydrate user sessions; if it's purely ephemeral non-reversible hashing and auto-expire in <24h we can support.

From a product standpoint: exposing per-model aggregate metrics is okay but we should bind it to a rate limit and specify the set of fields (latency_p50/95, error_code_counts, model_tag). We should avoid exposing prompt-level metadata or any inputs/outputs.

If Security is comfortable, I'll draft a conservative clause that limits fields, enforces 1-min rollup by default but can be adjusted to 5-min for high-volume routes, and requires MetricX onboarding controls.

— Priya
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Team — noted. Security position below:

- We can accept an observability export only if all of the following are contractually required:
  * MetricX must be engaged as a named subprocessor with a written subprocessor addendum and proof of SOC 2 Type II (shared with us prior to onboarding).
  * Exported fields limited to: model_tag, request_latency_ms_p50, request_latency_ms_p95, error_code, aggregated_count. No request/response content, no user ids, no IPs, no session ids.
  * Minimum aggregation window: 5 minutes by default; allow 1-minute rollup only after a documented risk assessment and customer opt-in with stronger controls.
  * Any hashed debug tokens must be non-reversible (salted one-way hash) and auto-expire in telemetry pipeline after 24 hours.
  * Explicit prohibition on using telemetry for model training without prior documented consent and an amendment to the DPA.

- Operational constraints: our KV cache and prefix-caching paths make 1-minute rollups expensive at high QPS; we should push for 5-min default with an escalation path that includes Product sign-off and cost-sharing for higher granularity.

If we accept BrightLayer's current redline language we'll need to counter with the points above. I'll draft security-friendly language and share.

— Irene
Head of Product Security
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Tom Bennett <tbennett@brightlayer.co>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, BrightLayer Legal <legal@brightlayer.co>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Tom — thanks for the redlines. Internal summary and proposed compromise attached (proposed_dpa_patch_redline.txt). High-level summary:

- Redwood can permit an observability export to MetricX limited to aggregated metrics only (model_tag, latency p50/p95, error counts, aggregated_count).
- Default aggregation window will be 5 minutes; we can provide a path to 1-minute rollup after a technical and security review (and agreed cost delta).
- MetricX must be named as a subprocessor and provide SOC2 Type II evidence prior to onboarding.
- Hashed debug tokens allowed only if non-reversible and auto-expire in telemetry pipeline within 24 hours.
- Strict prohibition on using telemetry to train models unless a separate amendment is executed.

Can you confirm if BrightLayer can accept the 5-minute default and the SOC2 requirement? If yes, we'll update the DPA with the proposed language for legal countersign.

Attachment: proposed_dpa_patch_redline.txt (text, 3KB)

— Mike
From: Tom Bennett <tbennett@brightlayer.co>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightLayer Legal <legal@brightlayer.co>, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-16T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: analytics export + observability subprocessor request

Mike + team — appreciate the pragmatic response and the proposed language. We can accept:

- 5-minute aggregation as the default; we'll open a ticket to evaluate 1-minute for a small set of routes in Q4 (no commitment today).
- MetricX named as subprocessor with SOC2 Type II evidence before onboarding.
- Hashed debug tokens must be non-reversible and auto-expire — acceptable.
- The no-training prohibition is fine; BrightLayer won't request telemetry for training without a formal amendment.

We reviewed the proposed_dpa_patch_redline.txt and legal is OK to move forward pending Redwood's final countersign. Please have legal send the final DPA.

Thanks — Tom
